title: General categorical-pattern model theorem with marked enrichment
statement:
Use categorical patterns $\mathfrak P=(C,S,\{p_\alpha\})$, $\mathfrak P$-fibered marked objects and $\mathsf M_{\mathfrak P}$ from [def-coef-categorical-pattern-fibrancy], the categorical model category $\mathsf K$ of marked simplicial sets from [lem-coef-marked-point-cartesian-model], and model categories and trivial maps from [lem-coef-model-infinity-derived-adjunction]. For every such small pattern there is a left proper combinatorial simplicial model structure on $\mathsf M_{\mathfrak P}$. Its cofibrations are exactly the maps injective on all underlying simplices, and its fibrant objects are exactly the $\mathfrak P$-fibered objects. Left proper means that pushout along a cofibration preserves weak equivalences; combinatorial has the meaning specified in [lem-coef-marked-point-cartesian-model].

For marked objects $A,B$ over $\bar C$, define the marked enriched Hom $\mathcal H_C(A,B)$ by
$$\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathrm{sSet}^+}(L,\mathcal H_C(A,B))=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathsf M_{\mathfrak P}}(A\times L,B)$$
for every marked simplicial set $L$, with the base map of $A\times L$ obtained by projection to $A$. Its underlying $n$-simplices are maps $A\times(\Delta^n)^\flat\to B$; an edge is marked when its associated map $A\times(\Delta^1)^\sharp\to B$ preserves markings. Put
$$\operatorname{Map}^{\sharp}_C(A,B)_n=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathsf M_{\mathfrak P}}(A\times(\Delta^n)^\sharp,B).$$
These are the mapping objects for the simplicial model structure; if $B$ is fibrant they are Kan complexes. A map $f:A\to A'$ is a weak equivalence exactly when $\operatorname{Map}^{\sharp}_C(A',Z)\to\operatorname{Map}^{\sharp}_C(A,Z)$ is a weak homotopy equivalence for every $\mathfrak P$-fibered $Z$.

The marked enrichment is tensored by $A\otimes L=A\times L$ over $C$, and cotensored by the objects representing $A\mapsto\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathrm{sSet}^+}(L,\mathcal H_C(A,B))$. It satisfies the marked enriched model axiom: for every cofibration $i:A\to A'$ in $\mathsf M_{\mathfrak P}$ and fibration $r:B\to B'$ there, the induced map
$$\mathcal H_C(A',B)\longrightarrow\mathcal H_C(A,B)\times_{\mathcal H_C(A,B')}\mathcal H_C(A',B')$$
is a fibration in $\mathsf K$, trivial when either $i$ or $r$ is trivial. Equivalently, for a cofibration $i:A\to A'$ of pattern objects and a cofibration $j:L\to L'$ in $\mathsf K$, the pushout product
$$(A'\times L)\amalg_{A\times L}(A\times L')\longrightarrow A'\times L'$$
is a cofibration of pattern objects, trivial if either factor is trivial.

source.place: Theorem B.0.20, Definition B.2.1, Remark B.2.6, Remark B.0.25 and Remark B.2.5 (second pattern trivial on a point). Gepner-Haugseng Theorem 3.2.5 and Remark 3.2.12 record precisely the fully scaled quasicategory case. Read online, not archived in literature/. No Stacks tag states this theorem.

proof.text:
Work in the slice $\mathsf M=\mathrm{sSet}^+_{/\bar C}$ defined in [def-coef-categorical-pattern-fibrancy], using marked internal Homs from [lem-coef-marked-point-cartesian-model]. Limits are formed on underlying simplicial sets with an edge marked exactly when every projection marks it; colimits are formed on underlying simplicial sets and mark the images of marked edges. Thus all small limits and colimits exist. Every marked object over $\bar C$ is the filtered union of its subobjects with finitely many nondegenerate simplices and their chosen markings. Maps from such a finite object are determined by finitely many simplex images and marking conditions, and equality of two such maps is witnessed at one common stage; thus its Hom functor preserves filtered colimits. There is a small set of these finite objects over the fixed small base. This proves local finite presentability directly. Monomorphisms are generated as a weakly saturated class $C_0$ by $(\partial\Delta^n)^\flat\to(\Delta^n)^\flat$ over all simplices of $C$, together with $(\Delta^1)^\flat\to(\Delta^1)^\sharp$ over the edges of $S$: first attach the missing underlying simplices in skeletal order, then add the remaining markings one at a time. Conversely these maps and their pushouts, transfinite composites and retracts are monomorphisms. Construct the marked Hom explicitly as
$$\mathcal H_C(A,B)=B^A\times_{\bar C^A}(\Delta^0)^\sharp,$$
where the point is the structure map $A\to\bar C$. The product/internal-Hom adjunction gives the required enriched-Hom bijection. For a marked $L$, the cotensor is
$$B^{L}_{C}=B^L\times_{\bar C^L}\bar C,$$
with $\bar C\to\bar C^L$ adjoint to projection. Its slice Hom bijection is $\operatorname{Hom}_{/\bar C}(A,B_C^L)=\operatorname{Hom}_{/\bar C}(A\times L,B)$. Composition, unit and tensor associativity are induced by evaluation and composition of the maps being represented. The degreewise description of $\mathcal H_C$ gives precisely the flat simplices and sharp marked edges stated in the item.

source.place: B.0.25 and B.2, proof of B.0.20; explicit marked slice constructions.

proof.text: Let $J=J_{\mathfrak P}$ and $\operatorname{An}_{\mathfrak P}$ be the concrete generating set and its weakly saturated closure of [lem-coef-pattern-anodyne-lifting-products]. This is a small set even for infinite $K_\alpha$: its indices are the given small family, the natural numbers, and sets of maps between small simplicial sets. Apply [lem-coef-accessible-small-object-factorization] to $J$ in the locally presentable slice from step 1, and to each terminal arrow $A\to\bar C$. Obtain a functor $E$ and natural $\eta_A:A\to EA$ in $\operatorname{An}_{\mathfrak P}$, with $EA$ lifting against $J$, hence $\mathfrak P$-fibered. For some regular $\kappa$, $E$ preserves $\kappa$-filtered colimits. Indeed the small-object middle functor has this property; the functor $A\mapsto(A\to\bar C)$ preserves these colimits because a filtered category is nonempty and connected, so the colimit of the constant terminal-object diagram is terminal. No claim that $E$ preserves all filtered colimits is made for infinite cones. Here $\mathfrak P$-fibered has the current four-clause meaning in [def-coef-categorical-pattern-fibrancy]: inner fibration, exactly the cocartesian edges over $S$ marked with the required lifts, a classifying limit diagram for each cone pullback, and a relative limit diagram for every cocartesian section. Both cone requirements are retained when $K_\alpha$ is empty; no closure or additional marking hypothesis on $S$ is imposed.

source.place: B.1.1, B.1.6; proof of B.0.20, replacement construction, with a sufficiently large regular cardinal for arbitrary small cones.

proof.text: Define $W$ by the sharp mapping test in the statement. By [lem-coef-pattern-anodyne-lifting-products], the test spaces are Kan, and every $\mathfrak P$-anodyne map belongs to $W$ since its restriction maps are trivial Kan fibrations. Two-out-of-three, isomorphisms and retract closure hold by applying the mapping tests. Naturality of $\eta$ and two-out-of-three imply $f\in W$ if and only if $Ef\in W$. By [lem-coef-pattern-fibered-edge-detection], this is equivalent to every $\Delta^1$-pullback of $Ef$ being a categorical equivalence.

source.place: B.2.1, B.2.2, B.2.4 and the replacement argument in the proof of B.0.20.

proof.text: By [lem-coef-categorical-equivalences-small-generation] and [lem-coef-joyal-filtered-equivalences], the full replete subcategory $\mathcal V$ of categorical equivalences in $\mathsf{sSet}^{[1]}$ is closed under small filtered colimits and generated under them by a small set $E_0$. Fix an uncountable regular $\lambda$. For each filtered presentation $X:J\to E_0$, apply [lem-coef-filtered-colimit-cardinal-regrouping]. It expresses its colimit as a $\lambda$-directed colimit of colimits of restrictions to filtered subcategories with fewer than $\lambda$ arrows.

source.place: Proof of B.0.20, accessibility/perfectness argument using edge pullbacks; sufficiently filtered Smith variant for arbitrary small cones.

proof.text: Each restricted colimit belongs to $\mathcal V$ by its filtered closure. These colimits have a small set $E_1$ of isomorphism representatives: replace each indexing category by a structure on an ordinal less than $\lambda$; its composition tables and all functors into the small full category on $E_0$ form a set, since the ambient Hom sets are small. Choose their colimits. Thus $E_1$ generates $\mathcal V$ under $\lambda$-filtered colimits. Every $\lambda$-filtered category is filtered, so $\mathcal V$ is closed under these colimits as well. This is precisely the subcategory-accessibility convention in [lem-coef-accessible-arrow-inverse-image].

source.place: Proof of B.0.20, accessibility/perfectness argument using edge pullbacks; sufficiently filtered Smith variant for arbitrary small cones.

proof.text: Define $F(A)=\coprod_{e\in C_1}(UEA\times_C\Delta^1)$, where $U$ forgets markings and each pullback uses its indicated edge $e$. By step 2, $E$ preserves $\kappa$-filtered colimits for some regular $\kappa$. The other operations preserve these colimits degreewise: forgetting markings retains the underlying colimit, and pullback of sets over a fixed set preserves colimits because it selects the fibers with a prescribed base label; coproducts commute with colimits by the universal property of compatible maps from each summand. Hence $F$ preserves $\kappa$-filtered colimits. Each summand is a quasicategory: $EA\to C$ is an inner fibration, so its pullback to the quasicategory $\Delta^1$ is an inner fibration with quasicategory domain. A coproduct of quasicategories is a quasicategory because every inner horn is connected and therefore maps into a single summand.

source.place: Proof of B.0.20, accessibility/perfectness argument using edge pullbacks; sufficiently filtered Smith variant for arbitrary small cones.

proof.text: Apply [lem-coef-quasicategory-labelled-coproduct-equivalences] to $X_e=UEA\times_C\Delta^1$ and $Y_e=UEA'\times_C\Delta^1$, indexed by $e\in C_1$, and to their maps induced by $Ef$. Step 6 supplies the quasicategory hypotheses and $F(f)$ preserves the label $e$ by construction. Hence $F(f)$ is a categorical equivalence exactly when every edge pullback of $Ef$ is one. The cited statement allows empty summands and the empty indexing set.

source.place: Proof of B.0.20, accessibility/perfectness argument using edge pullbacks; sufficiently filtered Smith variant for arbitrary small cones.

proof.text: Step 3 and the preceding component calculation give $W=F^{-1}(\mathcal V)$. Apply [lem-coef-accessible-arrow-inverse-image] to $F$ with source the locally presentable slice of step 1 and target simplicial sets. The latter is locally finitely presentable by the same finite-simplex argument of step 1 with no markings or base conditions. The preceding steps verify both accessibility of $\mathcal V$ in its specified convention and preservation of sufficiently filtered colimits by $F$. Consequently $W$ is accessible in the ambient arrow category. For the empty base, $F$ is constant empty and its equivalence test is vacuous, as required.

source.place: Proof of B.0.20, accessibility/perfectness argument using edge pullbacks; sufficiently filtered Smith variant for arbitrary small cones.

proof.text:
For a monomorphism $u:A\to B$, [lem-coef-pattern-anodyne-lifting-products] says that every $\operatorname{Map}^\sharp_C(u,Z)$ is a Kan fibration. Hence $u\in W$ exactly when each such map lifts all boundary inclusions, by [lem-coef-kan-quillen-right-proper]. By the cotensor bijection of step 1 this is exactly left lifting of $u$ against all
$$Z_C^{(\Delta^n)^\sharp}\longrightarrow Z_C^{(\partial\Delta^n)^\sharp},\qquad n\geq0,\quad Z\ \mathfrak P\text{-fibered}.$$
A left lifting class is closed under pushout by extending a square through the pushout, under transfinite composition by extending the lift at each successor stage and taking the prescribed colimit at a limit stage, and under retracts by inclusion and projection of squares. Intersecting with the similarly weakly saturated monomorphisms proves weak saturation of $C_0\cap W$. This is a statement about these cotensor maps, not an invocation of model axioms for a structure still to be built.

source.place: B.1.14 and the model-recognition argument in B.2; explicit weak saturation via cotensor lifting.

proof.text:
If $p:A\to B$ lifts all monomorphisms, lifting $\varnothing\to B$ gives a section $s:B\to A$. Lifting
$$A\times\{0,1\}^\sharp\hookrightarrow A\times(\Delta^1)^\sharp$$
against $p$, with endpoints $\operatorname{id}_A,sp$ and bottom map $p\operatorname{pr}_A$, gives a marked homotopy between these endpoints over $C$. Thus $p$ has a marked homotopy inverse. Precomposition on every sharp mapping simplicial set gives homotopy inverse maps: transpose the homotopy and use the same $\Delta^1$ parameter. These induce inverse maps on path components and all homotopy groups, so $p\in W$. Now [lem-coef-smith-model-recognition] applies: step 1 gives a small generating set and weak saturation of $C_0$, step 9 gives weak saturation of $C_0\cap W$, step 8 gives accessibility, step 3 gives two-out-of-three, and the preceding lift gives the final hypothesis. Obtain a combinatorial model structure with cofibrations $C_0$, weak equivalences $W$, and fibrations $(C_0\cap W)^\square$, with functorial factorizations.

source.place: Proof of B.0.20, condition (3) and model recognition; accessible Smith version.

proof.text: Every generator in $J$ is a monomorphism in $W$ by steps 2-3. Thus a model-fibrant object lifts $J$, and is $\mathfrak P$-fibered by [lem-coef-pattern-anodyne-lifting-products]. Conversely if $Z$ is $\mathfrak P$-fibered, every trivial cofibration $u$ induces a Kan fibration on the sharp mapping spaces by that same node and a weak equivalence by the definition of $W$. By [lem-coef-kan-quillen-right-proper] this is a trivial Kan fibration, so is surjective on vertices. Every map from the domain of $u$ therefore extends to its codomain. This says precisely that $Z$ is model-fibrant. All objects are cofibrant, since their initial maps are monomorphisms. Consequently the fibrant-object identification includes all four clauses of [def-coef-categorical-pattern-fibrancy], in particular both its classifying-limit and cocartesian-section relative-limit requirements, with the specified universes and empty cones allowed.

source.place: B.1.6, B.1.14 and proof of B.0.20, fibrant-object identification.

proof.text:
Consider a pushout of $f:A\to B$ in $W$ along a monomorphism $A\to A'$, with pushout $B'$. For each $\mathfrak P$-fibered $Z$, the tensor in step 1 preserves this pushout, so degreewise the sharp mapping spaces satisfy
$$\operatorname{Map}^\sharp_C(B',Z)=\operatorname{Map}^\sharp_C(B,Z)\times_{\operatorname{Map}^\sharp_C(A,Z)}\operatorname{Map}^\sharp_C(A',Z).$$
All these spaces are Kan, and $\operatorname{Map}^\sharp_C(A',Z)\to\operatorname{Map}^\sharp_C(A,Z)$ is a Kan fibration by [lem-coef-pattern-anodyne-lifting-products]. The map $\operatorname{Map}^\sharp_C(B,Z)\to\operatorname{Map}^\sharp_C(A,Z)$ is a weak equivalence by $f\in W$. Pulling this weak equivalence back along that fibration gives $\operatorname{Map}^\sharp_C(B',Z)\to\operatorname{Map}^\sharp_C(A',Z)$, which is a weak equivalence by [lem-coef-kan-quillen-right-proper]. Thus $A'\to B'$ lies in $W$, proving left properness of the constructed model structure.

source.place: Lemma B.2.3 and proof of B.0.20, left properness.

proof.text: We need a product argument for both factors of the marked axiom. First, any $W$-map $g:X\to Y$ between $\mathfrak P$-fibered objects has a marked homotopy inverse. In the mapping test with $Z=X$, surjectivity on $\pi_0$ supplies $h:Y\to X$ and a path from $hg$ to $1_X$. In the test with $Z=Y$, injectivity on $\pi_0$ and $(gh)g\simeq g$ imply $gh\simeq1_Y$. The spaces are Kan by [lem-coef-pattern-anodyne-lifting-products], so paths may be taken as edges; they are exactly maps with the parameter $(\Delta^1)^\sharp$. Conversely such inverse homotopies imply every mapping test is a homotopy equivalence by precomposition. This argument uses neither an underlying unmarked inverse nor vertexwise equivalence alone.

source.place: Lemma B.2.4, formal equivalence (1) with (2), and Remark B.2.5.

proof.text:
For $f:A\to B$ in $W$ and any marked simplicial set $L$, the maps $\eta_A\times L,\eta_B\times L$ are $\mathfrak P$-anodyne by the product assertion of [lem-coef-pattern-anodyne-lifting-products], with second factor $\varnothing\to L$. The map $Ef$ is a $W$-map between fibered objects, so has the inverse homotopies of step 13. Multiplying these homotopies by $L$ gives inverse homotopies for $Ef\times L$; precomposition shows it lies in $W$. Naturality of $\eta$ and two-out-of-three now imply $f\times L\in W$.
For the other factor, take a weak equivalence $j:L\to L'$ in the point model $\mathsf K$ of [lem-coef-marked-point-cartesian-model]. Apply the same small-object replacement to the trivial point pattern $\mathfrak P_0$. Its fibered objects are exactly quasicategories with their equivalences marked: over a point, cocartesian edges are equivalences and there are no cone conditions. The mapping definition of $W$ for this pattern is precisely that of $\mathsf K$. Thus $E_0j$ has marked inverse homotopies by step 13 for this pattern. For any pattern object $A$, the maps $A\times\eta_L,A\times\eta_{L'}$ are $\mathfrak P$-anodyne by the other half of the product assertion (first factor $\varnothing\to A$). Multiplying the inverse homotopies of $E_0j$ by $A$ and applying two-out-of-three gives $A\times j\in W$.

source.place: Remark B.2.5, replacement-and-homotopy-inverse proof, specialized to the trivial point pattern.

proof.text: Let $i:A\to A'$ and $j:L\to L'$ be monomorphisms in the pattern and point categories. Their pushout product $k$ is a monomorphism: in each degree its domain is the union of the two indicated subsets of $A'\times L'$. If $i$ is a weak equivalence, step 14 makes both $i\times L$ and $i\times L'$ weak equivalences. The map $A\times L'\to\operatorname{dom}(k)$ is the pushout of $i\times L$ along the monomorphism $A\times j$, so is a weak equivalence by step 12. Its composite with $k$ is $i\times L'$, hence $k\in W$ by two-out-of-three. If $j$ is a weak equivalence, instead the map $A'\times L\to\operatorname{dom}(k)$ is a pushout of $A\times j$ along $i\times L$ and its composite with $k$ is $A'\times j$; step 14 and left properness give the same conclusion. This proves the full marked pushout-product axiom, including either trivial factor.

Translate this to the Hom formulation. For the displayed induced map $t=\mathcal H_C(i,r)$ and a marked map $j$, the enriched Hom bijection identifies a lifting square $j\perp t$ with a lifting square $(i\square j)\perp r$. If $j$ is a trivial cofibration of $\mathsf K$, step 15 makes $i\square j$ a trivial pattern cofibration, so it lifts every pattern fibration $r$ by the model weak factorization systems of [lem-coef-model-infinity-derived-adjunction]. Thus $t$ is a fibration of $\mathsf K$, by the lifting characterization in [lem-coef-marked-point-cartesian-model]. If $i$ is trivial, the same holds for every point cofibration $j$ by step 15; if $r$ is trivial, $i\square j$ is a cofibration for every such $j$ and lifts $r$. The other model weak factorization system in $\mathsf K$ then makes $t$ a trivial fibration in either case. This proves the asserted marked enriched model axiom.

Finally apply the simplicial model axiom already present in the point model [lem-coef-marked-point-cartesian-model] with its initial cofibration $\varnothing\to(\Delta^0)^\sharp$. It says that $K^\sharp\to(K')^\sharp$ is a point cofibration for every simplicial cofibration $K\to K'$, trivial if the latter is trivial. Step 15 therefore gives the simplicial pushout-product axiom for the pattern tensor $A\times K^\sharp$. Its cotensor is $B_C^{K^\sharp}$ from step 1 and its mapping simplicial set is the sharp mapping object by its defining bijection. The represented composition and unit from step 1 give the enrichment, and [lem-coef-pattern-anodyne-lifting-products] gives the Kan assertion for fibrant targets. The model structure constructed in step 10 is consequently simplicial with exactly the mapping objects and weak-equivalence test stated in the item.
